extracted.intended_audience: owners/operators of CCR management units, facility environmental managers, environmental consultants, and state regulators
extracted.subtask_description: Requirements and performance standards for designing, installing, sampling, analyzing, reporting, and taking corrective action for groundwater monitoring at Coal Combustion Residual Management Units (CCRMU) to comply with 40 CFR part 257 (Groundwater monitoring and corrective action).

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability of existing groundwater monitoring and corrective action requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: CCRMU must comply with the existing groundwater monitoring and corrective action requirements in §§257.90 through 257.98, with one modification: combined detection and assessment monitoring.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA concluded there is nothing about CCRMU that makes them distinct enough to warrant separate groundwater monitoring requirements from other CCR units; commenters did not provide factual basis to treat CCRMU differently.

rubrics_metrics.name: Single deadline for groundwater monitoring requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: All groundwater monitoring requirements for CCRMU must be completed no later than 42 months after the effective date of the final rule (codified at §257.90(b)(3)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA adopted a single deadline (42 months) to provide flexibility for activities susceptible to external delays (weather, contractor shortages, permitting, seasonality) and to allow interested parties to verify compliance; May 8, 2028 is the codified example date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design and installation of groundwater monitoring system — performance standard
rubrics_metrics.description: The monitoring system must consist of a sufficient number of wells both upgradient and downgradient of the CCR unit, installed at appropriate locations and depths, to yield groundwater samples from the uppermost aquifer that accurately represent background groundwater quality and groundwater passing the downgradient waste boundary, monitoring all potential contaminant pathways (40 CFR 257.91(a)(1)–(2)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regulations do not prescribe exact number/location/depth because hydrogeologic conditions vary; minimums and site-specific characterization are required to meet the general performance standard.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum number of monitoring wells
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulation requires installation of a minimum of one upgradient and three downgradient wells.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Additional wells necessary to achieve the general performance standard must be installed; the number/placement must be based on site-specific information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Site-specific determination of well number, spacing, and depth
rubrics_metrics.description: Number, spacing, and depth of monitoring wells must be determined based on site-specific information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider thorough characterization of aquifer thickness, groundwater flow rate, groundwater flow direction throughout seasonal/temporal fluctuations, the unit's geological and hydrogeological setting, and other site conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of existing monitoring wells
rubrics_metrics.description: Existing monitoring wells can be used as part of the CCRMU groundwater monitoring systems provided the wells meet the Federal criteria.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Owners/operators should ensure existing wells meet construction, placement, and representativeness criteria before relying on them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Well construction, operation, maintenance, and protection
rubrics_metrics.description: Monitoring wells must be cased, constructed, operated, and maintained in a way that preserves the integrity of the monitoring well borehole, screened interval and other components so as to ensure the well performs to the design specifications throughout the life of the monitoring system.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Owners/operators should adequately protect wells from activities that may damage them (livestock, vehicles, machinery) and otherwise adversely impact performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documentation and operating record requirements for monitoring system
rubrics_metrics.description: Design, installation, development, and decommissioning of any aspect of the groundwater monitoring system must be thoroughly documented and included in the operating record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Documentation should be sufficient for verification and long-term recordkeeping; see additional annual report and data requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: P.E. certification or Participating State/EPA approval
rubrics_metrics.description: The owner or operator must obtain a P.E. certification or approval from the Participating State Director or EPA stating the groundwater monitoring system meets the standards set out in §257.91.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Certification/approval documents should be included in the operating record and support that the installed system meets regulatory performance standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Groundwater sampling and analysis plan contents (§257.93)
rubrics_metrics.description: The owner or operator must develop a groundwater sampling and analysis program that satisfies §257.93 and includes: a list of monitoring wells to be sampled (the monitoring network); the schedule for sampling; sampling procedures and techniques; sample preservation and shipping protocols; analytical procedures including an appropriate statistical method for analysis; and quality assurance and quality control (QA/QC) methods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The plan must include all analytes listed in Appendix III and Appendix IV; EPA guidance documents (e.g., RCRA Groundwater Monitoring: Draft Technical Guidance, 1992; Low-Flow Ground-Water Sampling Procedures, 1996) contain recommended procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of Appendix III and Appendix IV analytes in sampling/analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Sampling and analysis plan must include all analytes listed in Appendix III and Appendix IV.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA recommended analytical procedures and QA/QC controls can be found in cited EPA guidance documents; combined monitoring will require collection of containers for both appendices at each sampling event.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection and justification of statistical procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Owners/operators must select statistical procedures that will be used for evaluating groundwater monitoring data as part of the sampling and analysis program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA recognizes the importance of statistical independence and appropriate sampling frequency; sampling too frequently can create non-independent, autocorrelated samples undermining required statistical analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowable approaches to represent background groundwater quality
rubrics_metrics.description: Owners/operators are allowed to collect background groundwater samples as far upgradient as needed (even offsite) to ensure samples are not impacted by CCR, and may collect background samples at other representative wells when hydrogeologic conditions do not allow determination of hydraulically upgradient wells.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA has not found situations where representing background groundwater quality was impossible; facilities must provide factual basis if claiming infeasibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Combined detection and assessment monitoring requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA requires sampling and analysis of constituents listed in Appendix IV at the same time as those listed in Appendix III (combined detection and assessment monitoring) for CCRMU.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale: expedites initiation of assessment monitoring and corrective action where units are likely already contaminating groundwater; combined monitoring collects the same Appendix III information while providing more data on Appendix IV constituents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Laboratory and resource considerations for combined monitoring
rubrics_metrics.description: Combining Appendix III and Appendix IV constituents into one sampling plan will not require additional field mobilizations but will increase the number of sample containers per well and may increase laboratory throughput burden.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA acknowledges increased demand on labs and contractors due to combined monitoring but considers the incremental reporting/evaluation burden minor and justifies extended single deadline to accommodate backlogs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collection of eight independent baseline samples
rubrics_metrics.description: Owners/operators must complete sampling and analysis of a minimum of eight independent samples for each background and downgradient well as required by §257.94(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA finalized this requirement to be completed no later than the single deadline (42 months after the effective date); baseline samples are necessary to initiate detection and assessment monitoring.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing for identification of statistically significant increases (SSIs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Within 90 days after initiation of the detection monitoring program, owners/operators must identify any SSIs over background levels for constituents listed in Appendix III (as required by §257.94).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Initiation of the assessment monitoring program (e.g., establishing groundwater protection standards and evaluating for SSLs of Appendix IV constituents) should proceed to expedite corrective action when warranted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial and annual groundwater monitoring and corrective action report deadlines
rubrics_metrics.description: Owners/operators must comply with §257.90(e) which requires preparation of an annual groundwater monitoring and corrective action report no later than January 31 of the year following the calendar year after a groundwater monitoring system has been established, and annually thereafter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA rejected delaying the initial report until after collection of baseline samples; the annual report serves as an update on monitoring program activities including installation of wells.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required content of annual monitoring and corrective action report
rubrics_metrics.description: The annual report must contain specific information identified in the regulations, including but not limited to: maps; aerial images or diagrams showing the CCRMU and all upgradient (background) and downgradient wells; identification of any monitoring wells installed or decommissioned in the previous year; monitoring data collected under §§257.90 through 257.98; and a narrative discussion of any transition between monitoring programs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Groundwater quality sampling data should be included in appendices and summarized/tabulated in the report; exceedances (SSIs and SSLs) should be tabulated/highlighted when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Baseline and supporting data to be included in annual report
rubrics_metrics.description: Annual reports must contain the basic data which informs positions and status, including but not limited to boring logs, monitoring well installation diagrams, water level data, field sampling data sheets for groundwater sample collection, laboratory analytical data including QA/QC data, and data validation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These data should make clear the basis for compliance conclusions and enable public review and verification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organization and public accessibility of annual reports
rubrics_metrics.description: Annual groundwater monitoring and corrective action reports should be organized so that: (1) compliance with the CCR regulations is evident; (2) data supporting compliance conclusions are easily located within the document; and (3) the public is readily able to review the groundwater monitoring data and related information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report must be posted on the public CCR website with a clear file name and be readily printable/downloadable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Validation of well locations and flow direction annually
rubrics_metrics.description: Upgradient and downgradient well locations and depths should be validated annually with respect to measured and mapped groundwater flow directions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Annual report should tabulate and analyze groundwater level data to determine flow directions and groundwater levels relative to any residual CCR left in place.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification of nearby receptors in annual reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Annual reports should identify the nearest downgradient surface water bodies as well as groundwater supply wells in the vicinity of the unit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This information helps inform risk evaluation and corrective action decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corrective action trigger and requirements for Appendix IV exceedances
rubrics_metrics.description: If groundwater monitoring demonstrates an exceedance of the groundwater protection standards (GWPS) for constituents identified in Appendix IV, corrective action is required as laid out in §§257.96 through 257.98.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combined monitoring expedites identification of Appendix IV exceedances, which in turn expedites ASD (Assessment of Source and Determination) development or corrective action as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sampling frequency and seasonality considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Sampling and characterization schedules must account for seasonal variability in groundwater flow, groundwater levels, and constituent concentrations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA acknowledges that seasonality, protected species, clearing restrictions, permitting delays, and other temporal constraints may affect when field activities can occur and used these factors to justify the single extended deadline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accounting for contractor, laboratory, and permitting constraints
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA recognizes that limited availability of qualified contractors, laboratory backlogs, and permitting/approval delays can impede timely compliance and has extended deadlines and allowed flexibility accordingly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Owners/operators should plan for potential third-party delays and document efforts and constraints in the operating record and reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intrawell data comparisons — allowance and caveats
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA will not prohibit use of intrawell groundwater data comparisons for CCRMU despite commenter requests; intrawell comparisons are permissible but EPA acknowledges they have been misused.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA expects owners/operators to justify appropriate statistical approaches; intrawell comparisons may be limited in applicability (e.g., pre-placement background) but are not categorically barred.
